newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS - Absa lifts profit, market unimpressed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Absa lifts profit, market unimpressed.

text.p: Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) on Monday unveiled 25 percent growth in 1996/97 earnings per share and promised better results from the current year despite margin pressures.

But the market was unimpressed, focussing on the tough environment now facing South African banks. Investors wiped 600 million rand ($134.1 million) off Absa's market capitalisation as the shares took a knock.

"We look forward to ongoing real growth in earnings through responsible and profitable asset growth and further improvement in the ratio of costs to income," said group chief executive Danie Cronje on the release of year figures.
But he added that the group expected its relatively high net interest margins to continue falling to a level of about four percent from 4.28 percent for the year ended March 31, 1997.

The banking group's headline earnings per share totalled 222.2 cents in the year against 178.0 cents in 1995/96. That came as a disappointment to analysts who had forecast earnings per share at a consensus 225.5 in a range of 223.0-228.8 cents.
Cronje admitted second half earnings growth had been hard won in a banking environment made increasingly competitive by disintermediation.

"The first six months was a very good six months in terms of growth. That was not the experience in the second half...Margins were as much as 30 percentage points lower than in the first six months," he said.

Despite Cronje's earnings growth pledge, investors gave Absa's lower-than-expected earnings result the thumbs down, highlighting poor lending growth and weakening market share as key areas of concern.
"The loan growth was very disappointing. I don't think Cronje came up with a response to either maintain market share or try and get some of it back," said one analyst.
The market agreed and Absa shares, which were up 10 cents before the results, closed down one rand at 28.75 rand.
"Their results are a little bit weaker than what the market expected and that's why the share is now slipping," one dealer said.
Cronje was apologetic about group loan growth, which fell to 12.6 percent from 16.3 percent last year.
"The one area that we felt that last year we did not achieve what we set out to do is in the mortgage side," he noted.

Cronje blamed the performance on competition from aggressive niche players and local banking major Standard Bank Investment Corp as well as the banking group's conservative approach to new debt products, such as tied credit cards.
"There is a lot of growth there that we did not take part in," he said, adding it was crucial that Absa arrest the decline in lending market share.
"In the long run this is the one that we really have to make sure that we maintain our market share in to enable us to produce the profits that we need," he said.
Absa increased its bad debt provisions to 760 million rand from 538 million rand a year ago, a move Cronje said was prudent given the tougher economic environment facing South Africa.
"It would be wrong not to make appropriate provision during this very difficult time in the cycle of the economy," Cronje said.
Absa had been hit by defaults in several areas including installment financing, mortgage finance, especially in township areas, and in its factoring and invoice discounting arm, Cutfin.
But Cronje said bad debts were not concentrated in any particular arm or client of Absa with no specific provisions above 50 million rand in value.
-- Johannesburg newsroom +227 11 482-1003 ($ = 4.475 South African Rand)
